claims.text: EPFL study management regulations provide two formal procedures to oppose a grade or notified failure: an internal request for reassessment at EPFL within 10 days, or an external appeal to the Commission de recours interne des EPF within 30 days. Both deadlines are calculated from reception, at the address given by the student, of the grade or notified failure (transcripts sent by post). If a mark is contested on the grounds of an error in correction or assessment, the responsible teacher is the only person authorized to modify the mark subject to justification to the program direction; if contested for a formal defect, Legal Affairs reviews whether a significant formal defect impacted the result to warrant exam cancellation and repetition. Procedural costs are charged ahead of the procedure and refunded only if the student's claim succeeds. These rules govern academic grade disputes; whether specific appeal pathways or different deadlines apply to AI disciplinary misconduct sanctions is not established on this page and remains an evidence gap.

claims.claimText: EPFL study management regulations provide two formal procedures to oppose a grade or notified failure: an internal request for reassessment at EPFL within 10 days, or an external appeal to the Commission de recours interne des EPF within 30 days. Both deadlines are calculated from reception, at the address given by the student, of the grade or notified failure (transcripts sent by post). If a mark is contested on the grounds of an error in correction or assessment, the responsible teacher is the only person authorized to modify the mark subject to justification to the program direction; if contested for a formal defect, Legal Affairs reviews whether a significant formal defect impacted the result to warrant exam cancellation and repetition. Procedural costs are charged ahead of the procedure and refunded only if the student's claim succeeds. These rules govern academic grade disputes; whether specific appeal pathways or different deadlines apply to AI disciplinary misconduct sanctions is not established on this page and remains an evidence gap.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: There are two ways of opposing a grade or notified failure: a procedure at EPFL, called request for reassessment, and a procedure outside of EPFL, through the Commission de recours interne des EPF, called appeal.

privacy_data.zh: EPFL 建议学生切勿将机密、隐私或个人信息输入外部公开生成式 AI 工具，因为数据将与私营企业共享且失去控制。在已采集的 EPFL 教学指引中，通过 EPFL 账户使用的企业许可（如 Microsoft 365 Copilot）被描述为不适合处理受监管数据，因为该指引称 EPFL 尚未签署确保数据保护措施符合机构需求或瑞士个人数据保护法的数据处理协议（DPA）；本次审查未独立核实当前中央 IT 合同或租户 DPA 状态。

approved_tools.en: EPFL lists official educational AI services including AI Tutors (CEDE) deployed within participating courses, aiaiapps for teachers, and the internal EPFL Chatbot. Microsoft 365 Copilot is listed with allowed availability, but tool directory listing does not constitute assessment permission or a verified current IT DPA.
approved_tools.zh: EPFL 列出了官方教学 AI 服务，包括在参与课程中部署的 AI Tutors (CEDE)、面向教师的 aiaiapps 以及校内 EPFL Chatbot。Microsoft 365 Copilot 处于允许可用状态，但工具目录列出并不构成考核使用许可，亦不代表已确认当前中央 IT DPA。

research_publication.en: EPFL Library guidance clarifies that LLMs cannot be listed as authors or co-authors under the Swiss Copyright Act (Art. 6) because they lack accountability. Under EPFL Library's agreement with Elsevier, CC-BY open access content may be used with any AI tool, whereas for licensed closed or CC-BY-NC-ND publications, use is permitted with closed non-learning AI tools or with open learning tools operating in a secure, user-controlled environment (on-premises or solely for authorized users); commercial use is prohibited and publications must not reproduce closed or CC-BY-NC-ND content.
research_publication.zh: EPFL 图书馆指引明确说明，依据瑞士著作权法（第 6 条），LLM 因无法承担责任而不能列为作者或合著者。依据 EPFL 图书馆与 Elsevier 的协议，CC-BY 开放获取成果可用于任何 AI 工具；而对于订阅期刊受限内容或 CC-BY-NC-ND 成果，仅允许在不参与训练的封闭式 AI 工具中或在用户控制的安全受控环境（本地自建或仅限授权用户）中运行的学习型工具中使用；禁止商业用途，且生成结果不得复制封闭或 CC-BY-NC-ND 原文内容。

academic_integrity.en: Submitting AI-generated content as one's own work without proper attribution constitutes AI plagiarism under Lex 1.3.3 Article 4. AI detection tools are not admissible as stand-alone evidence due to false-positive risks; teacher referral of suspected non-disclosure to the section director and Legal Affairs is a misconduct evaluation referral, not an adjudication of cheating. Formal grade or notified failure disputes follow EPFL study regulations: internal reassessment within 10 days or external appeal to the Commission de recours interne des EPF within 30 days calculated from postal reception of the grade or notified failure; these rules govern academic grading disputes, and whether specific appeal pathways apply to AI disciplinary misconduct sanctions is an unverified evidence gap.
academic_integrity.zh: 依据 Lex 1.3.3 第 4 条，将 AI 生成内容作为本人作品提交且未适当归属构成 AI 抄袭。因存在较高误报风险，AI 检测工具不能单独作为抄袭证据；教师对疑似未披露情况向系主任及法务部门的报告属于行为性质评估移送，而非直接认定作弊。正式成绩或不及格通知争议遵循 EPFL 学习管理规定：在收到学业成绩或不及格书面邮寄通知后 10 天内申请校内重评，或 30 天内向 EPF 内部申诉委员会提出外部申诉；此程序适用于学业成绩争议，针对 AI 纪律处分的具体申诉途径仍属未核实的证据缺口。

teaching_guidance.en: EPFL teaching guidance recommends that because there is no one-size-fits-all rule regarding the use of AI in assessment, teachers make explicit to students what kind of AI use is not legitimate in their course and what rules accompany the use of AI tools.

topicBasis.approved_tools: EPFL lists official educational AI services including AI Tutors (CEDE) deployed within participating courses, aiaiapps for teachers, and the internal EPFL Chatbot. Microsoft 365 Copilot is listed with allowed availability, but tool directory listing does not constitute assessment permission or a verified current IT DPA.
topicBasis.research_publication: EPFL Library guidance clarifies that LLMs cannot be listed as authors or co-authors under the Swiss Copyright Act (Art. 6) because they lack accountability. Under EPFL Library's agreement with Elsevier, CC-BY open access content may be used with any AI tool, whereas for licensed closed or CC-BY-NC-ND publications, use is permitted with closed non-learning AI tools or with open learning tools operating in a secure, user-controlled environment (on-premises or solely for authorized users); commercial use is prohibited and publications must not reproduce closed or CC-BY-NC-ND content.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: Submitting AI-generated content as one's own work without proper attribution constitutes AI plagiarism under Lex 1.3.3 Article 4. AI detection tools are not admissible as stand-alone evidence due to false-positive risks; teacher referral of suspected non-disclosure to the section director and Legal Affairs is a misconduct evaluation referral, not an adjudication of cheating. Formal grade or notified failure disputes follow EPFL study regulations: internal reassessment within 10 days or external appeal to the Commission de recours interne des EPF within 30 days calculated from postal reception of the grade or notified failure; these rules govern academic grading disputes, and whether specific appeal pathways apply to AI disciplinary misconduct sanctions is an unverified evidence gap.
topicBasis.teaching_guidance: EPFL teaching guidance recommends that because there is no one-size-fits-all rule regarding the use of AI in assessment, teachers make explicit to students what kind of AI use is not legitimate in their course and what rules accompany the use of AI tools.
topicBasis.security_procurement: Central IT procurement terms, vendor compliance standards, and institutional data processing protocols for third-party artificial intelligence tools are not established in reviewed public evidence.

do.en: Check course outlines and consult instructors regarding permitted AI use before using tools for studying or coursework; ensure assessment material that is not your personal and original contribution is recognizable as such under LEX 1.3.3 Article 4, where the studying guide states AI tool use should be disclosed in a statement and directs students to check the course policy or instructor for its formulation.

do.en: For manuscripts intended for publication, disclose the LLM tool used, its purpose, and method in the manuscript adhering to publisher policies.
do.zh: 对于拟发表的手稿，依据图书馆指引在手稿中披露所使用的 LLM 工具、具体用途及使用方式，并遵守出版社规定。

do.en: For disputes over an academic grade or notified failure, request internal reassessment within 10 days or appeal to the EPF internal appeals commission within 30 days, both from postal receipt at the student’s address. These deadlines have not been verified as AI disciplinary appeal deadlines.
do.zh: 对于学业成绩或不及格通知的争议，可在邮寄通知送达学生地址并收悉后 10 天内申请校内重评，或在收悉后 30 天内向 EPF 内部申诉委员会申诉。这些期限未被核实为 AI 纪律处分的申诉期限。

dont.en: Students should not use generative AI tools during exams or assessments unless explicitly allowed by the course policy or instructor.
dont.zh: 学生在考试或考核中不应使用生成式 AI，除非课程规定或教师明确允许。

draft-claim-epfl-grade-reassessment-appe.text: EPFL study management regulations provide two formal procedures to oppose a grade or notified failure: an internal request for reassessment at EPFL within 10 days, or an external appeal to the Commission de recours interne des EPF within 30 days. Both deadlines are calculated from reception, at the address given by the student, of the grade or notified failure (transcripts sent by post). If a mark is contested on the grounds of an error in correction or assessment, the responsible teacher is the only person authorized to modify the mark subject to justification to the program direction; if contested for a formal defect, Legal Affairs reviews whether a significant formal defect impacted the result to warrant exam cancellation and repetition. Procedural costs are charged ahead of the procedure and refunded only if the student's claim succeeds. These rules govern academic grade disputes; whether specific appeal pathways or different deadlines apply to AI disciplinary misconduct sanctions is not established on this page and remains an evidence gap.

evidence.quote: There are two ways of opposing a grade or notified failure: a procedure at EPFL, called request for reassessment, and a procedure outside of EPFL, through the Commission de recours interne des EPF, called appeal.

The deadline to start these procedures is within 10 days for the request for reassessment and within 30 days for the appeal. Both deadlines are calculated from the reception, at the address given by the student, of the grade or notified failure (transcripts sent by post).
